CELLS TO LIFE

A visual journey through the female reproductive system, the menstrual cycle and the remarkable process of fertilization.

A system designed for life

The female reproductive system produces ova, secretes hormones and provides the structures needed for fertilization and pregnancy.

01 · Main role

Ova production

The ovaries contain developing follicles and release an ovum during ovulation.

02 · Hormones

Estrogen & progesterone

These hormones help regulate the menstrual cycle and prepare the uterine lining.

03 · Fertilization

Meeting point

Fertilization usually occurs in the ampulla of the uterine (fallopian) tube.

04 · Pregnancy

Support & nourishment

If implantation occurs, the uterus supports the developing embryo.

Meet the main organs

Each structure has a distinct role, working together as one coordinated system.

Ovaries

Paired organs that contain follicles, release ova and produce estrogen and progesterone.

Fallopian tubes

Carry the ovum toward the uterus. Fertilization most often takes place in the ampulla.

Uterus

A muscular, hollow organ where an embryo may implant and develop during pregnancy.

Endometrium

The inner lining of the uterus. It thickens during the cycle and is shed during menstruation if pregnancy has not occurred.

Cervix

The lower, narrow part of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

Vagina & vulva

The vagina is an elastic canal; the vulva refers to the external genital structures.

Reference infographic: reproductive organs, hormones and fertilization overview.

The menstrual cycle

A cycle is counted from the first day of one menstrual period to the first day of the next. 28 days is an average, not a rule.

1

Menstrual phase

The uterine lining is shed, causing menstrual bleeding.

2

Follicular phase

FSH supports follicle development. Estrogen helps rebuild the uterine lining.

3

Ovulation

A surge in LH triggers release of an ovum from the ovary.

4

Luteal phase

The corpus luteum produces progesterone, helping maintain the endometrium.

Key hormones

FSH: stimulates ovarian follicle development. LH: triggers ovulation. Estrogen: supports growth of the endometrium. Progesterone: helps prepare and maintain the uterine lining after ovulation.

How fertilization happens

Fertilization is the union of a sperm cell and an ovum, restoring the diploid chromosome number.

1

Sperm reaches the ovum

Sperm travel through the female reproductive tract toward the uterine tube.

2

Penetration

One sperm passes through the surrounding layers and fuses with the ovum membrane.

3

Nuclei unite

The maternal and paternal genetic material come together.

4

Zygote forms

The fertilized cell begins cleavage as it travels toward the uterus.

Important structures

Sperm: head (acrosome and nucleus), middle piece and tail/flagellum. Ovum: corona radiata, zona pellucida, cell membrane, cytoplasm and female genetic material.

The journey at a glance

Follow the sequence from ovulation to the beginning of embryonic development.

Ovulation→Ovum enters tube→Fertilization→Zygote→Cleavage→Blastocyst→Implantation

Fertilization usually occurs in the ampulla of the uterine tube. Implantation normally occurs in the endometrium.
